requirement:
[p206]     9.23.     GOV-023 Guardrail Definition and Management Authority
[p206] 
[p206] 
[p206] Only authorised administrative or policy-management users may create, modify, activate or
[p206] deactivate organisational pricing guardrails.
[p206] 
[p206] A Guardrail is a configured organisational pricing constraint used to evaluate whether
[p206] proposed pricing work remains within an acceptable pricing boundary.
[p206] 
[p206] A Guardrail must remain distinct from:
[p206] 
[p206]    ● approval authority;
[p206]    ● approval-routing thresholds;
[p206]    ● workflow-routing rules;
[p206]    ● policy-authorisation eligibility;
[p206]    ● user permissions;
[p206]    ● initiative-specific assumptions or commercial targets.
[p206] 
[p206] Supported organisational guardrails for the MVP may include, where applicable:
[p206] 
[p206]    ● minimum gross-margin threshold;
[p206]    ● maximum discount;
[p206]    ● maximum price increase;
[p206]    ● maximum price decrease;
[p206]    ● maximum absolute or percentage price movement;
[p206]    ● another supported pricing constraint that can be evaluated from structured pricing
[p206]        information.
[p206] 
[p206] Each configured Guardrail must identify, where applicable:
[p206] 
[p206]    ● persistent Guardrail identifier;
[p206]    ● name or human-readable description;
[p206]    ● guardrail type;
[p206]    ● metric or pricing condition being evaluated;
[p206]    ● operator or comparison rule;
[p206]    ● threshold or configured value;
[p206]    ● applicable organisational or Pricing Scope;
[p206]    ● applicable pricing dimensions where relevant;
[p206] 
[p207]    ● behavioural treatment;
[p207]    ● effective date or effective period where relevant;
[p207]    ● active or inactive status.
[p207] 
[p207] Supported behavioural treatment must follow GOV-025.
[p207] 
[p207] A Guardrail may apply organisation-wide or to a supported organisational or pricing scope.
[p207] 
[p207] Where more than one Guardrail applies to the same pricing work, each applicable Guardrail
[p207] must remain separately identifiable and evaluable.
[p207] 
[p207] Guardrail configuration must not itself determine whether a Pricing Proposal is Approved,
[p207] Rejected or Authorised Within Policy.
[p207] 
[p207] Approval authority, approval-routing thresholds and policy-authorisation qualification remain
[p207] governed by their respective workflow and governance requirements.
[p207] 
[p207] The system must preserve enough configuration information for the analytical layer to
[p207] evaluate applicable Guardrails deterministically where the required pricing inputs are
[p207] available.
[p207] 
[p207] Where a Guardrail cannot be deterministically evaluated from supported structured
[p207] information, the product must not invent a result or treat the Guardrail as satisfied.
[p207] 
[p207] Consequential Guardrail configuration changes must be attributable, auditable and
[p207] historically traceable in accordance with GOV-034.
[p207] 
[p207] Changes to a Guardrail must apply prospectively according to the applicable governance
[p207] and Proposal-version rules and must not silently reinterpret the Guardrail configuration
[p207] preserved with an already submitted Pricing Proposal version.
[p207] 
[p207]

[p208]    ● review;

title: Guardrail Behavioural Treatment
requirement:
[p208]     9.25.      GOV-025 Guardrail Behavioural Treatment
[p208] 
[p208] 
[p208] Each configured Guardrail must have a supported behavioural treatment that determines the
[p208] governance consequence of a confirmed Guardrail Breach.
[p208] 
[p208] Supported MVP treatments must include:
[p208] 
[p209] Warning
[p209] 
[p209] A confirmed Breach may continue through the pricing process where other applicable
[p209] requirements are satisfied, but the Breach must remain prominently visible to relevant users
[p209] and within the decision record.
[p209] 
[p209] Approval Escalation
[p209] 
[p209] A confirmed Breach requires the pricing work to follow the configured higher or additional
[p209] approval path before organisational decision authority can be established.
[p209] 
[p209] Approval Escalation must not itself grant approval authority or determine which user may
[p209] approve the pricing work.
[p209] 
[p209] Applicable approval authority and routing remain governed by the workflow and approval
[p209] requirements.
[p209] 
[p209] Blocking
[p209] 
[p209] A confirmed Breach prevents the affected pricing work from progressing beyond the
[p209] applicable controlled gate until:
[p209] 
[p209]    ● the pricing work is changed so that the Guardrail is no longer breached; or
[p209]    ● an explicitly supported governance path permits progression under organisational
[p209]        policy.
[p209] 
[p209] A Guardrail evaluation state of Within Guardrail must not trigger an adverse Guardrail
[p209] treatment.
[p209] 
[p209] Unable to Evaluate must remain distinct from a confirmed Breach.
[p209] 
[p209] Where a Guardrail is required for a consequential decision and its evaluation state is Unable
[p209] to Evaluate, the system must not treat the Guardrail as satisfied.
[p209] 
[p209] The applicable Proposal, workflow or policy-authorisation requirement must determine
[p209] whether pricing work with an Unable to Evaluate result may progress.
[p209] 
[p209] Guardrail behavioural treatment must be configured through governance and must not be
[p209] redefined independently by the Pricing Builder, analytical layer, workflow or AI.
[p209]

title: Governance Configuration Versioning and Historical Context
requirement:
[p214]     9.34.     GOV-034 Governance Configuration Versioning and Historical Context
[p214] 
[p214] 
[p214] Consequential governance configuration must remain historically traceable.
[p214] 
[p214] The system must preserve consequential changes to supported governance configuration
[p214] including:
[p214] 
[p214]    ● roles;
[p214]    ● permissions;
[p214]    ● approval authority and limits;
[p214]    ● Guardrails;
[p214]    ● workflow policies;
[p214]    ● scope assignments;
[p214]    ● policy-authorisation configuration and conditions.
[p214] 
[p214] For each consequential governance configuration change, the system must preserve, where
[p214] applicable:
[p214] 
[p214]    ● affected configuration object;
[p214]    ● persistent configuration identifier;
[p214]    ● configuration version or revision;
[p214]    ● previous configuration state;
[p214]    ● resulting configuration state;
[p214]    ● responsible user;
[p214]    ● change timestamp;
[p214]    ● effective date or effective period where relevant.
[p214] 
[p215] For Guardrails specifically, each consequential configuration state must remain identifiable
[p215] through the persistent Guardrail identifier and the applicable configuration version or
[p215] revision.
[p215] 
[p215] A change to a Guardrail threshold, operator, applicable scope, behavioural treatment,
[p215] effective period or active status must create historically distinguishable governance
[p215] configuration.
[p215] 
[p215] Submitted Pricing Proposal versions must remain associated with the exact governance and
[p215] Guardrail configuration that formed part of their controlled decision snapshot.
[p215] 
[p215] A later governance configuration change must not silently rewrite:
[p215] 
[p215]    ● an earlier Proposal decision snapshot;
[p215]    ● the Guardrail evaluation preserved with that Proposal;
[p215]    ● a historical approval or policy authorisation;
[p215]    ● the governance context under which an earlier decision occurred.
[p215] 
[p215] Where a changed governance configuration must affect active pricing work, the resulting
[p215] treatment must be explicit, attributable and auditable and must follow the applicable
[p215] Proposal, workflow and governance requirements.
[p215] 
[p215] Historical pricing decisions must remain sufficient to determine which governance
[p215] configuration applied at the relevant time.
[p215] 
[p215]

[p216] 
[p216] For any consequential pricing action, Owómidé must be able to determine:
[p216] 
[p216] Who performed the action?
[p216] What role and authority did they possess?
[p216] What resource were they acting on?
[p216] Was that resource inside their permitted scope?
[p216] Which guardrails applied?
[p216] Was separation of duties respected?
[p216] What governance configuration existed at that time?
[p216] 
[p216] If the system cannot answer these questions reliably, the pricing action is not sufficiently
[p216] governed.
[p216]

[p217] 
[p218]                   10. AI ASSISTANCE AND AI GOVERNANCE

[p218] 
[p218] It must assist users inside the pricing workflow rather than operate as a separate chatbot
[p218] detached from pricing context.
[p218] 
[p218] AI may help users interpret, construct, analyse and navigate pricing work, but authoritative
[p218] pricing data, deterministic calculations, governance decisions and consequential actions
[p218] must remain controlled by the product and authorised human users.
